progress_update.summary: Designed a unified linking model from scratch through an extensive design conversation. Started on promise-objects branch fixing proto bugs, then evolved the entire linking architecture through collaborative design. Arrived at a clean model: objects and workflow invocations are the two node types, objects are the only anchors, four link combinations, ServiceEdges/InvocationEdges tables. Wrote and reviewed the design doc on a new linked-services branch forked from main.
progress_update.goal: Design and implement linked services: object-to-object linking with completion/GC (Phase A), then workflow invocation linking (Phase B). Objects as persistent anchors, workflow invocations as ephemeral unless anchored.
accomplished: Fixed proto field numbers and LinkCommand message type ID (0x040F→0x0415) on promise-objects branch
Added command/notification type ID offset test to prevent future mismatches
Designed unified linking model through collaborative design session: two node types (Object/WorkflowInvocation), NodeId enum, four link combinations, one anchoring rule
Designed storage schema: evolve VirtualObjectStatus (add Completed), new ServiceEdges ('se') and InvocationEdges ('ie') tables, EdgeState enum on LinkedTo edges, LinkedFrom as presence-only
Designed complete message flow: LinkServiceCommand/Request/Response, CompleteServiceCommand, ServiceCompletionNotification, UnlinkServiceCommand/Request with GC cascade
Wrote comprehensive design doc at docs/design/linked_services.md covering Phase A (object linking) and Phase B (invocation linking)
Reviewed and addressed all plan review items: Completed+Locked conflict, cycle detection, proto type IDs, LinkedFrom value spec, invocation rejection
progress_update.now: Design doc committed on linked-services branch. Ready for implementation planning and task breakdown for Phase A.
next_steps: Create implementation plan and task breakdown for Phase A (object linking)
Implement ServiceEdges table (KeyKind, key schema, read/write traits, RocksDB implementation)
Implement LinkServiceCommand, CompleteServiceCommand, UnlinkServiceCommand journal commands + proto + codec
Implement outbox messages and state machine handlers (on_link_service_request, on_service_completion_notification, on_unlink_service_request)
Tests: link establishment, object completion with onCompleted, state/invocation rejection, GC cascade
constraints: All tables are logical (2-byte KeyKind prefix) within one RocksDB CF per partition — no write amplification from multiple tables
NodeId enum (Object/WorkflowInvocation) used consistently across all messages for forward compatibility with Phase B
ServiceCompletionNotification and InvocationResponse are orthogonal — graph management vs result delivery
Completed objects reject new invocations entirely at the inbox
Direct cycle detection only (point read) — transitive cycles cause GC leak but not correctness issue
Proto type IDs assigned: LinkService=0x0415/0x8015, CompleteService=0x0416/0x8016, UnlinkService=0x0417
decisions: Two node types: NodeId::Object(ServiceId) and NodeId::WorkflowInvocation(ServiceId, InvocationUuid)
One anchoring rule: live objects are the only anchors
VirtualObjectStatus: Unlocked | Locked(InvocationId) | Completed(ResponseResult) — three mutually exclusive states
Separate edge tables by local node type: ServiceEdges and InvocationEdges — table IS the discriminator
Use existing ServiceInvocation pathway for Phase B (option C) with linked marker, not a new outbox message
Unlink (not RemoveLink) as the verb for edge removal
Phase A (object linking) ships independently from Phase B (invocation linking)
New branch linked-services forked from main — clean implementation without promise-objects branch baggage
open_questions: Should workflow invocations get invocation-scoped KV state in addition to journal?
Batch GC optimization — batching UnlinkServiceRequest per destination partition
handle.getOutput() for objects — how does a workflow await an object's completion result? Likely via AttachInvocation-like mechanism
